title: Government, Society and Economy
description: A general studies introduction to the social sciences: the study of politics and the concept of government, forms of government, law, democracy and good governance in Nigeria, economics and development, and ICT in the social sciences.

topics.title: The Study of Politics and the Concept of Government
topics.summary: Political science is the systematic study of politics, which has no single definition but always involves power, influence and authority. Government is the administrative apparatus of the state, whose four characteristics are a population, a defined territory, a functional government and sovereignty.
subtopics: Definitions of politics: Aristotle, Lasswell, Easton
History and significance of the study of politics
Scope of political science and levels of politics
Power, influence and authority (traditional, charismatic)
Theories of the origin of the state
Elements of the modern state

topics.title: Organisation and Classification of Government
topics.summary: Governments are classified by who rules and in whose interest (Aristotle's six forms), by how power is distributed (unitary, federal, confederal), by the structure of the executive (presidential, parliamentary, dual), and by ideology (capitalism, socialism, communism).
subtopics: Arms of government and separation of powers
Aristotle's classification: good and perverted forms
Unitary, federal and confederal government
Presidential, parliamentary and dual executive systems
Capitalism, socialism and communism
Lijphart's typology and other forms of government

topics.title: Law, Democracy and Good Governance in Nigeria
topics.summary: Law is a body of official rules found in constitutions, legislation and judicial opinions that governs a society and controls behaviour. It keeps public order, enables co-operation, confers legitimacy, upholds rights and duties and communicates standards, and it underpins democracy and good governance.
subtopics: Definitions of law (Black's Law Dictionary, Austin)
Constitutional sovereignty, security and welfare, and citizens' duties
Functions of law
Law and morality
Substantive and procedural, public and private, civil and criminal law
Customary law; democracy and good governance

topics.title: Economics and Development
topics.summary: Economics studies how scarce resources with alternative uses are allocated to satisfy unlimited wants, which forces choice and creates opportunity cost. Economic growth is a rise in productive capacity and national income, while economic development is broader, including the reduction of poverty, inequality and unemployment.
subtopics: Scarcity, choice and opportunity cost
Production, consumption, distribution and exchange
The law of demand
Definitions of economics: Smith, Mill, Marshall, Robbins
Economics as a science; models
Economic growth versus economic development

topics.title: ICT and the Social Sciences in the 21st Century
topics.summary: The social sciences study human relationships as systematically as the natural sciences study nature. ICT, which replaced the term IT in the early 1990s, supports social science teaching and learning through learning about, with and through ICT, information literacy, independent learning and new learning theories.
subtopics: Natural sciences and social sciences
What ICT is
Learning about, with and through ICT
ICT in the social science disciplines
Basic issues: effectiveness, cost, equity, sustainability
ICT, information literacy and independent learning
